Vision Support - SeeAbility
Pupil Support
Vision Support - SeeAbility
Clive Efford visits to meet SeeAbility
On Friday 13th December, Marjorie McClure School had a visit from our local MP, Clive Efford, who came to see the amazing work SeeAbility do to support our students and their families. Over the past few years SeeAbility have become an integral part of the holistic offering at Marjorie McClure and it has enabled families to access vision support services at school.
About SeeAbility – a 225 year old charity
SeeAbility is a national charity that works with people with learning disabilities and autism, many of whom will have sight loss. They are 225 years old this year. Their work in eye care is to improve access to eye care for all people with learning disabilities. Most people with a severe learning disability will have a sight problem. Many sight problems can be treated and supported but people with learning disabilities often miss out, including on access to sight tests and glasses.
SeeAbility provide information and advice, including in ‘easy read, employ eye care champions with lived experience to improve experience and access to local opticians and employ our own clinical team.
This clinical work started in 2013 in special schools. They found half of children in special schools have a sight problem, most commonly a need for glasses, yet only 1 in 10 children had ever gone for their sight test at an opticians. The vast majority of children were either under hospital eye clinics or had never had any eye care at all.
SeeAbility have delivered over 8000 sight tests since 2013, presenting the evidence to NHS England and becoming the biggest global study of its kind, winning national awards.
Marjorie McClure is well known for embracing innovation and was one of the first schools to get access to the NHS funded ‘proof of concept’ eye care service 2021 when SeeAbility began its work. The impact of eye care at Marjorie McClure has been transformative for the children.

Welcome to FE
In our FE provision, we focus on creating a supportive, personalised pathway for every learner. We build programmes around each student’s strengths, interests and needs, helping them develop the life skills, confidence and independence that matter most to them. Through a mix of practical subjects, community experiences and work‑related opportunities, students are encouraged to achieve in ways that feel meaningful and achievable.​
We work closely with families and professionals to provide gentle transition support, ensuring each young person feels secure as they move towards their next steps. Our aim is to help every learner grow at their own pace, feel included in their community, and begin their journey into adulthood with confidence and pride.
FE life is exciting – it is the opportunity to spread your wings, try new things and be more independent.

Welcome
Our School
Head Teachers Welcome
Welcome to Marjorie McClure School, a school where we believe that learning is an adventure, one filled with inspirational, creative opportunities and a variety of experiences to enable every individual to grow and become their best self.
Marjorie McClure is an outstanding special school for students with complex medical needs and physical disabilities. We cater for students from 4-19 years old. All students must have an EHCP in place to attend.
I have been Head Teacher at Marjorie McClure since September 2019, and it is a great privilege and pleasure to work with such amazing students, families and staff. Our school really is a family, and we endeavour to support our broader community.
At Marjorie McClure we value the broad scope of learning and achievement, with a personalised curriculum richly embedded with aspects of development in communication, independence, life skills and social skills as well as the traditional academic areas. We celebrate every step of achievement and recognise the significance of small steps.
We embrace a multi-agency approach and work closely with the nursing team, speech and language therapists, occupational therapist and physiotherapists that are based here at Marjorie. We have an exceptional team of teachers, advanced skills assistants, teaching assistants and health care assistants who are highly specialised, offering highly specialised education and care.
In April 2023, we moved into a fantastic new purpose-built site. The new facilities have been specially designed to meet the needs of our students and include a wheelchair friendly outside play area, a sensory room, an immersive room, soft play room and rebound therapy room. In May 2024, we were the very lucky recipients of a Chelsea Flower Show garden which takes pride of place. This year we are celebrating our Golden Anniversary as it is 50 years since the opening of Marjorie McClure School.
In September 2024 we joined the Nest Academy Trust and are excited to embrace this new partnership.
Paula Farrow - NEST CEO - Welcome
Dear Staff, Parents and Carers,
We are delighted to announce that Marjorie McClure School, has officially joined the family of Nexus Education Schools Trust group of schools, as of the 1st September 2024.
At NEST, we value exceptional and distinctive learning communities, and the diversity and ethos of each school. Each school, its leaders and staff bring something to the wider organisation and enable our schools to be supported by knowledgeable and talented people, who are committed to providing an inclusive diverse and engaging curriculum for each child. Marjorie McClure joins our adventurous and innovative schools, who collaborate in a range of creative curriculum events such as musical, drama and sporting occasions to give the children in each school the opportunity to feel part of the larger family of NEST schools.
NEST also incorporates Thames South Teaching School Hub, specialising in career development for support staff and teachers. The Trust is also fortunate to include specialist ASD (Autism) provision and has also recently opened its first NEST Nursery. NEST is an outward looking Trust, working in partnership with other Multi Academy Trusts, schools, and Local Authorities, further developing our offer to pupils, staff, and communities.
All NEST schools are committed to and have a proven track record of rigorous school improvement; where Headteachers and other leaders work together to share best practice and learn from one another as well as from other external networks and partnerships.
Our twenty schools across four local authorities are all different and aim to serve their local communities.
The Trust is ambitious for its schools and communities and, values the importance of having talented staff members within the Trust. In working together and contributing both expertise and innovative ideas, staff will enjoy opportunities to flourish professionally in our schools, supporting NEST’s growth and development.
NEST keeps students and pupils at the centre of all that it does - it is for their future, their education, and their achievements that this organisation will continue to be motivated to drive our work in years to come.
We are all looking forward to the exciting journey ahead.
CEO Nexus Education Schools Trust
Chair of the Local Committee Welcome
I think that the greatest privilege of being Chair at Marjorie McClure School is being able to see the school in operation during a normal school day. The huge energy that fills the building as the amazing staff work with our students every day, making their learning journey exciting and moulded to the abilities of each and every child. Since becoming involved with the school, we have had to cope with the complexities of the Pandemic and how to maintain a mixture of on campus and remote learning. I have huge admiration for the staff across the whole school in the way that they coped with this and in some ways I think that this has made the school more resilient.
Rebecca Cottage and the rest of the Senior Leadership Team have made many changes to the curriculum and also to the communication, both within the school and with families, making it much easier for staff and families to follow the progress of each student throughout their journey through the school.
On behalf of everyone on the Local Committee, thank you for taking the time to look through our website and hope that it gives a good insight into what we have to offer
Chair of the Local Committee

Personal Development
PSHE lessons equip pupils with the practical life skills, emotional understanding and self‑advocacy they need to thrive within school and beyond. Through carefully scaffolded learning about feelings, routines, safety, self‑care and the wider world, pupils build confidence in expressing preferences, managing daily challenges and making informed choices. This subject supports holistic wellbeing, nurtures independence and plays a crucial role in preparing our young people for adulthood and active participation in their communities.
Life Skills lessons play a vital role in preparing our pupils for everyday life. These sessions focus on teaching the practical, meaningful skills that young people need to confidently and independently access the world around them. Pupils learn essential areas such as managing finances, developing personal independence, making safe and informed choices, and building confidence in daily tasks like cooking and household routines. Through hands‑on, relevant learning experiences, our Life Skills curriculum empowers pupils to become more independent, capable, and prepared for their future—both within school and beyond.

Curriculum Pathways
Throughout the school, pupils are supported through one of four curriculum pathways, matched carefully to their developmental stage and age. All children joining us in Reception begin within the Early Years Foundation Stage (EYFS), where the Early Learning Goals, outcomes from EHCPs and individual interests shape a highly personalised curriculum.
As pupils move into Key Stage 1 (KS1), they transition to either the Sensory Pathway or the Practical Pathway, depending on the approach that best meets their learning needs. Most pupils continue within their chosen pathway from KS1 through to KS4, with progress closely monitored to ensure the curriculum remains the right fit. Where beneficial, we support pupils to move between pathways so that their provision always reflects their needs and aspirations.
At the end of Year 11, pupils transition into our Further Education (FE) Pathway, where they continue their learning journey until the end of Year 14, focusing on independence, personal development and preparation for adulthood.
